Oh, I actually wanted to talk to you about that. He's not coming with us, is he? I find him unprofessional, he doesn't take anything seriously. He won't stop bothering me, and who knows what could happen if we let our guard down...
Yeah, he's coming with us. It might also do you some good to loosen up a bit.
Yeah... You're right. I should stop standing guard and sit down for a while.
Ask for relief duty later, no problem with that.
Understood, Viktor! Come find me if you need anything.
See you.
(Interaction) What do you think of Viper?

Seems like a reliable guy, I always listen to what he has to say. I don't know how long he's been in the Zone but he seems to know a lot about what it takes to be a good stalker. If he told me to run straight into a pack of dogs, I'd do without hesitation.
Good to know.
(Interaction) Hey, Rookie. Wanted to ask — what do you think of Doggo?

He intimidates me a little, but he seems like one hell of a fighter. If he can carry that massive weapon, I'm sure he could go 1v1 against a big boar and come out on top. I'd put my money on him. \n When things on the North settle down, we could take him to the Duty arena and make a killing betting on him. Haha.
Not a bad idea, heh.
(Travel Requirement) Relax, Rookie. I need to ask you something.
Sorry, Viktor. The thought of Monolith guys showing up out of nowhere makes me nervous. What did you have in mind?
It's about your suit. It's just a basic jacket, right? I think you're going to need something better for the trip.

Glad you brought it up. I didn't know how to bring it myself, but honestly yes, it does worry me. \n Captain Kir had some spares, they belonged to guys who filled the Duty ranks but then deserted with a dishonorable discharge after getting scared off by the hardships. The suits were practically brand new... Think you could get them? Kir won't listen to me, he's been a bit cold towards me lately, but I'm sure he respects you, Viktor.
I'll go talk to him. Stay on guard duty.
(About the Suit) I got what we needed.
Now that's good news. I've been wanting to wear one of these suits for a while. I'm going to look like a real soldier now! Thanks a ton, Viktor.
Don't mention it. Get yourself ready for the trip in the meantime.
Hey, newbie. Got questions about how to be an expert stalker? You've come to the right place.
Hey, thanks for saving me. Damn ghosts...
How's it going, Stalker? I'm guarding so the others can get some rest.
(Task) Hey. I'm looking for a stalker's grave, shaped like a cross with a gas mask on it. You know wher-

(Doggo interrupts you) Pfffft. Newbie, the Zone is full of graves. I've counted about a thousand on my expeditions and I'm not exaggerating. I could list them one by one but we'd be here for hours, so I'll just say no. Go ask someone who's got time for that.
... Alright.
(Task) I'm looking for work. Need help with anything?
Yeah, rookie. I need help, but I doubt you're qualified.
What's it about?

I don't fear any mutant, not even bloodsuckers; the Zone's toughened me up over the years. But the other day something horrible happened... I got attacked by some fucking ghosts. They wouldn't stop screaming and making horrible sounds, it was really rough. I dropped my favorite weapon and ran away. I want to go back and deal with it. Would you come with me?
I think I can handle that.
Better if we go later.
You may not have the experience, but you've got balls and I like that. Let me grab my pistol and we'll go... A fucking PM. What an irony, seeing a veteran like me with gear like this, right?
I guess so... Let's get moving.
(Task) Ugh... Listen kid, I don't think I can walk straight. Could you ome with me to the base please? We'll find my weapon later, don't worry about that now.
You're not gonna die on me, are you?

Of course not. There's no tougher man than me in the Zone. But those ghosts really fucked my head... I'm seeing double, man. Give me a second and then cover me on the way back to camp... Think you can keep up?
Obviously. I've already proven I'm not just some rookie.
Keep up? Please don't go sprinting on me. I'm carrying a lot of weight.
(Task) I don't think there were actual ghosts. It was because of the mutant dwarf.
Listen, rookie, how long have you been in the Zone? It's been 7 years for me. I know how to tell the difference between a mutant and a supernatural experience.
...Whatever you say.
Anyway, here. You played your cards well, for a rookie. The real loss here is my weapon...
Why not just buy another one like it? Was it really that unique?

Rookie, you see these servomotors? They're built specifically to carry the weight of my weapon: 12 kilograms of pure power; she's one of a kind in the Zone. Her name is Linda, a modernized, upgraded, one-of-a-kind PKM Pecheneg I took off from a Monolith soldier who nearly killed me... I need to find her again at any cost. Without her I'm nothing.
I could help you look for her.
I don't think you could carry her on your own, runt. So bring a big backpack or something. If you find her, I'll be in debt forever.
...Ok. You know who I could ask?
Not sure... You could try asking Sidorovich, but he'll want bandit patches in return. So better go prepared.
Alright, see you.
(About Doggo's Weapon) Guess what I brought back.
Your rookie balls that you lost?
No, you idiot. Your weapon, I found it.

ARE YOU SERIOUS!? I can't believe it. My Linda, finally back with daddy. Here, friend, you've earned this. I have to admit I completely underestimated you. New or not, you're one hell of a stalker. From now on nobody's gonna mess with you, you hear me? You're under my protection.
Don't mention it.
(Interaction) I need to cross Darkscape and head north. Would you come with me?
Rookie, without my weapon I can't go anywhere. The Zone's been way too strange lately and it's dangerous even for a veteran like me. Once I get my gear back I'll think it over.
I understand.
(Interaction) I need to go through Darkscape and head north. Would you come with me?
Of course! But let's get more people together first, to improve our chances. Take that as advice from a veteran, friend.
We're already putting a group together. Come with me and I'll introduce you.

Hold on, let me load up the weapon and then we go, ok? I'm also bringing a few ammo boxes so we don't run short. You running a 5.45 caliber weapon? I've got plenty of that, so ask me if you need some.
Good. I'll wait for you and then we move.
(Interaction) Hey Doggo, what do you think of Viper?
I respect him.
That's it? Don't be shy.

Keep this between you and me, stalker. When I was working for the mercs, there was an important contract where they sent us to kill a lot of low-profile stalkers who I later found out were decent people. That's when I stopped working as a hired gun. One of the most wanted was Viper, seems like he left the Zone when he found out they were after him. The mercs killed almost all of his friends... That was one of the many losses Clear Sky suffered. First, everyone at the Nuclear Plant died, and then, someone pays millions to wipe out whoever's left. No doubt a group with rotten luck. Although lately I've been seeing more of their people walking around.
...I had no idea about any of that.
(Interaction) Have you had a chance to talk to Rooster?
Yeah, he's alright. Friendly guy, and he can sing...
That's it?

No. He did something weird a while ago. He saw me unpacking the box of 5.45x39 ammo and came to ask me for some, even though he's got an SGI rifle. That rifle uses 5.56 ammo, you know? I don't get why he asked me for the other kind if he can't even fire it with that weapon. Anyway, setting that aside, people who've been in Duty tend to be well trained. I know that.
Interesting...
(Interaction) What do you think of Rookie?

I went to offer him a relief shift so he could relax while I kept guarding, because he looked way too wound up. You know how he reacted? He jumped out of his skin when I spoke to him and yelped. Rooster couldn't stop laughing at him, haha. Anyway, if he's wearing that suit, it means that he's trained and knows how to fight; or at least I hope the rookie knows first aid.
You can always keep learning new things...
Don't you worry about that, Stalker. I'm going to make a great stalker out of you.
(That's not what I meant...) Thanks, Doggo.
What's up...?
(Task) Hey, I'm looking for a cross-shaped grave with a gas mask on it. Have you seen it?
Hmmm. No, no idea. But you can ask Fanatic, I know he's big on respecting the dead, he'd probably know something.
I see, thanks.
(Task) I'm looking for a stalker called Atreo. You know him?
No, I already heard you muttering about that with the others. I have no idea.
Understood. Bye.
(Task) Listen, stalker... Someone came to harass me a little while ago. A guy called Hook. Do you know him?

Well, he seems to know you. He was furious and almost hit me thinking I was "Viktor, the Thief." I spoke to Viper about it and he said you might be the one he was looking for, that's why I'm telling you.
I see.

Anyway, I don't want any trouble. This person told me he left a little gift for you in the backpack that's over that fireplace, and he insisted me that I told you to read his note... That's how you'll find him.
Understood, thanks for the message.
(Task) Have you seen Screw?
I saw him a few hours ago, he looked scared. Don't know what happened to him after that.
Did he say anything last time you saw him?

Hmmm... Let me think. 
 I'd collected payment for one of my jobs so I had some money... I went to see Sidorovich! 
 Came back after buying a few things from the old man. 
 I sat down and said hello to Screw, but he didn't answer. 
 He was muttering something while frantically going through his PDA, but I can't remember what it was. 
 Before I knew it, he'd rushed off in a hurry.
I see... Thanks.
(Task) I'm looking for a stalker who goes by "Atreo." You know where I can find him?

Good luck with that search, newbie. Atreo constantly changes his alias and his appearance to slip into the camp. Last time we caught him, he was calling himself "Ivyr" while faking a Nordic accent, the son of a bitch. I shot at him once and missed, then I had a clear shot but that pain in the ass Fanatic stopped me from pulling the trigger... He hasn't shown up around camp since.
So he got run out of camp... That's useful.
I wouldn't go in there if I were you.
What? Why?
Someone stole Gaucho's bread and they're looking for whoever did it. Things are real tense in there...
All that over a piece of bread?

That's right. Out here in the Zone, sharing bread with a stranger is how you make a new friend. It carries unspoken value, on top of the carbs. Having your bread stolen means things could end up in a gun fight...
THEY'RE GOING TO KILL EACH OTHER?
Nah, I'm messing with you. Go in and see if you can find it.
(Interaction) Any idea where the bread might be?
Not a clue. Gaucho doesn't want us leaving until it turns up, so we're gonna be stuck here for a while. If you find out who has it, let him know.
Sure. I'll let you know.
Your turn, friend.

Viktor. We were sorting things out and dividing up supplies. If you need ammo talk to Doggo, if you need medicine talk to Rooster, and if you've got the patience, talk to Rookie; he's a nervous wreck right now. When we're ready, let me know and I'll give the order.
Nice suit... As for the trip: are we forgetting anything?
I made sure we've got everything we need, friend. Don't worry about that. Should we head out? Or do you want to talk to the others first?
Let's go.
Hold on, I want to talk to them first.
What's my job here?

Listen Viktor, you're the stealthiest one among us, and the fastest. Doggo and I are going to provide you with covering fire so you can advance tree by tree and get close enough to the bastard. It's not the most efficient way, but it's the safest.
Alright, let's do it.

Ok. I'll be giving you directions over the communicator, stay sharp. You can only move while we're firing, that way we'll cover you and draw their fire. Don't take too long between trees or they'll spot you when we duck down, and that won't end well.
Waiting for your signal.

Viktor. Give me a second, I know you're in a hurry but I'm old and keeping up with you is hard. You can look around the area in the meantime, maybe there's a Monolith stash or something else that's useful.
(Interaction) Where should I look for something useful?
Not sure, friend. You're the climber. Maybe check the rooftops or anything up high? The rocks? I don't know. I'll call you soon so we can keep moving, don't wander too far. I'm waiting on a message.
Ok.
Are we moving out?
Yes, right now. We were waiting on you. Move out, everyone! (Viper looks visibly uneasy)
Let's go!
The mutant didn't hurt you, did it?
I'm fine. I think Rooster got the worst of it.

Maybe, but he'll be alright. See that drainage pipe up ahead? There are several paths, look carefully at which one we're taking and don't lose sight of me, so you learn the route in case you need to come back. Clear?
Got it. I'm right behind you.
Viktor! I was stretching my legs.
I need some medicine for the road.
Sure, here! These are the ones we scientists use. You can use them for radiation too.
Thanks, Rooster.
Friend! How's it going? I'm doing great, haven't seen this much action since I left Duty.
(Interaction) Glad to hear it. What were you checking with the detector just now?

This little guy started beeping for an artifact, but the only anomalies I can see are these electrical ones. I'm going to check what's out there, there's probably something we can't spot with the naked eye around here... Give me a minute!
Ok... I'll look around too.
Hey there, Stalker. I'm eager to turn whatever crosses our path into ashes.
Viper told me you had ammo.
Of course I do, and the good one. With armor-piercing, these boys tear through bulletproof vests and exoskeleton plating alike.
Great. Thanks, Doggo.
Hey Stalker. What you did with the sniper was flawless, well done. Stay sharp and watch my moves. If you're any good, you'll learn a lot from me.
(Interaction) ...Sure, I'll be watching. How are you holding up? Did they hurt you?

I'm in perfect shape, stalker. If you're looking for someone who got hit, check on those Monolith guys; though I doubt any of them survived Linda. By the way, did you know I was there when we took down this helicopter?
Really? When was that?

Four or five years ago, back when I still worked with Wolfhound's mercs. We had a contract to bring down three helicopters piloted by the military, they carrying scientists with sensitive data. My job was to come here to Darkscape with my unit, another group was sent to the Rostok factory, and the third group went to Yantar... On our end, we did everything "peacefully"; didn't kill anyone since it was a decoy helicopter to let the others get through safely. But I know the Wolfhound group made a massacre over there, and then they got killed by a stalker... That left me out of work for quite a while.
Four or five years ago? I was barely a teenager back then, I can't even imagine...
Don't worry about age, stalker. You're going to go far, Linda and I will go with you.
Thanks, Doggo. With your help I'm sure I'll get far.
Viktor. I'm kinda nervous, the silence on this side of the Zone is profound. Not a soul to be heard... I'm scared of screwing up. What would you recommend to calm down?
Relax, Rookie, we're a solid group. Everyone's gonna be fine.
I know the others are good fighters... But I'm not sure that's my strong suit. Should I head back to Cordon?
(Trust in Corporal) If you haven't found your strong suit yet, we'll figure it out along the way. Don't worry.
(Trust in the Group) Calm down, Rookie. We're a good group, we'll have your back.
(Rookie goes quiet for a moment) Thank you, I feel a lot better now, friend.
Thank you, Viktor. I just hope I'm not a burden...
Don't mention it. Stay sharp now, we're moving.
Viktor! Did you see me take out that group? I took your advice to heart and not one of them got away.
(Interaction) You did great spotting that sniper before any of us did. Very attentive of you.

Really? Thank you! Coming from you that means a lot. I've been thinking about ditching the Saiga and getting a decent sniper rifle down the line. What do you think? In Duty they didn't let anyone to just get their hands on those long-range weapons, so I got used to what I could get.
It'd be useful. A sniper would save us a lot of trouble.
I don't think it'll be necessary, we move just fine without one.
Alright, with your approval. If we pass by the bar later on I'll try to get my own rifle... I won't let you guys down.
Got it, Viktor. I won't stress about it then.
Perfect. See you later, and take a rest while you can.
How are you holding up, friend? You made it in one piece?
How do we track down Atreo now?
"How do we track someone who's slippery" is never a simple question. But right now, we've got an added difficulty layer on top of the usual.
Which one?

You know where you're standing? I trust your instincts as a scout, but this is nothing like the Cordon. The Dark Valley is a place of bandits and people who make their living hurting others. And on top of that, it looks like someone's been hunting them. So we might end up caught in the middle of a dispute that has nothing to do with us. But, well... we've got somewhere to start.
Talking to the bandits? But they must hate us.

I doubt it's personal; although you've built a reputation hunting them in Cordon. But they don't have to know that Viktor himself just walked into their backyard. Look around the area and look for a suit. I think that, if you dress like one of them, you could get close to their base and dig up more information. Someone must have seen Atreo arrive; the bastard's hard to miss.
That's true. I'll check everything and see what I can find.
Good. Did you make it alright? What are you going to do now?

I'm going to get this place organized. We need to set up patrols, do some reconnaissance, check our supplies, and maybe I'll try to get this generator running so we have some light, and so Rooster could set up a few sensors. \n Hopefully you can investigate without too much interference. We'll be pretty busy for now, but if you need backup, come back and take one of the guys with you. Sounds good?
Good, I'll take it easy then. Take care of yourselves.
No, you take care of yourself, friend. You're heading into places where the sun doesn't shine, so go in with some humility. If you need rest, ammo or medicine, come back and talk to the guys.
I'll be back when I have news or when I need something.
Listen, friend. I have a few questions for you before you get back to business.
What's going on?

You've seemed very agitated since we arrived. I thought you'd relax a little like the rest of us, but you haven't stopped for a second. And the others are thinking the same thing... We all have our reasons for being here, but we can't stop wondering: why is it so urgent for you to go after Leto? Does he owe you money or something?
Yeah, he owes me something. (Lie)
It's more complicated than a debt. (Tell the truth)
I don't have time for this. (Avoid the question)
What does he owe you? I can see you're willing to go to hell to get it... Must be worth a lot.
He stole an artifact from me.
And it was that important?
It is to me.
I see... Alright, I'll let you go, friend. Ituca's waiting for you.
See you.
What is it? You can trust me. You don't have to do this alone, friend.
I've been having visions for months... very intrusive dreams about coming to the Zone to find a specific place. When I found it, I discovered that Atreo had stolen something I was supposed to find.
What did he steal?
A very powerful artifact, with my name on it. It's mine.
How do you know it's yours?
Because of this. (Show Nox's note)

Well. Now that's a twist. I remember reading about this Nox in the files and documents that Clear Sky kept. As fas as I know, he used to be an "infiltrated" monolith who was eventually discovered and punished, but there must be more to it than that. We should go and investigate the Swamps base at some point.
I had no idea they had a base there...
Faction secrets, friend. Everyone's heard the rumors but the route is classified. Don't worry, I'll take you there later, just make sure you stay in one piece first. Alright?
Good, I'll be anxiously looking forward to that. I really need to find out more about Nox.
We'll investigate for everything we need. For now I'll let you free, head out and find your artifact. I'll keep things in order around here.
Thanks, friend. I'm going to talk to Ituca.
Listen, Viktor. We need answers. We all think highly of you and we genuinely want to help, but if you won't let us, there's nothing we can do.
I'm sorry, I have to go talk to Ituca.
Hey friend, what's going on?
Good thing we all made it in one piece. But what now?
How are you doing, Rookie?

I'm good and I'm happy. We made it without too much trouble and I've been having a great time with you guys... I thought the trip was going to be a lot more dangerous. I was even afraid I wouldn't be alive to tell the story.
I think we got lucky.
I think we did really well.
True, we should stay humble and grateful. I don't know what I would've done if something had happened to any of you...
That's life in the Zone. Let's stay alert for now.
You're right, Viktor. I'll get back to my guard post. Take care.
Good. See you later.

I know! That's what I thought, but I didn't want to say it out loud. Every time I feel like I'm doing things right, Doggo shows up and scolds me for letting my guard down. I get that he does it to train us and to keep us safe, but he doesn't let me enjoy the moment.
Doggo did great, but so did you. When you spotted that sniper before any of us did, that was flawless.
The credit's yours for dodging bullets between those trees. That was incredible, Viktor. I hope to keep learning from all of you. But I should get back to guard duty now. We'll talk later, friend.
Good. Later, Rookie.
I love Zone's bread. I'd like to meet whoever makes it.
How do you manage to eat with your gas mask on?

Pffft, sometimes I forget you're still on your first steps in the Zone, stalker. You lift your mask with the edge of the bread and take a bite, all in one quick move to avoid breathing in whatever crap is in the air. Got it? Practice that later.
...I'll give it a shot when I have time. Anyway, I wanted to ask how you came back. Are you in one piece?
Ask that to the others. But you can ask me how many monolith soldiers fell to my lethal shots.
Well, I guess that means you're fine.
Come on, stalker. Ask me how many.
How many fell to your lethal shots?
I'm glad you're in one piece. See you later.

Good question, glad the curiosity got to you. There were eight who had the fortune on the trip. I say fortune because it was an instant death. My shots always go straight to the center of the head, because I consider myself merciful.
Wouldn't expect anything less. Enjoy your bread, Doggo.
Damn, I got stuck on guard duty.
How's it going, Rooster?
I'm sleepy, really sleepy. The second my shift's over I'm going to sleep for an entire year.
You'll get your rest soon enough.
I've got an energy drink here. Is it helpful?

You can say that again. By the time I get to Yantar, I'm gonna have my eye bags on the floor, and the scientists will lose their minds saying I'm low on vitamin D and iron and all that. You know what iron supplements do? They make you shit black.
It isn't just helpful, you saved me with this, friend. Thank you.
That's disgusting.
It's nothing. Take care of yourself and don't let your guard down.
Stalker! Please don't shoot. I swear on my mother I'm not a bad person, I swear.
Thanks for letting me stay. If you need anything fixed, leave it to me.
One thing at a time. First, what happened here?

I'm not sure. We had a hideout and suddenly they hit us hard. There were shots from every direction. I played dead, obviously, and as soon as it stopped I came to hide. A while ago I heard footsteps that turned out to be you guys, that's how you found me like this. I don't want any more trouble. I already watched all my guys die.
Who shot at you?

I don't know, it all happened so fast. About ten seconds and BAM, everyone dead. I think the shots were coming from the North and the West, from all sides. There must have been twenty people shooting at us!
Anything else? Did you hear anything strange, something that might be useful?
I think I heard them praying when they finished their shooting... But it wasn't Christian, it was a different kind of prayer.
Were they Monolith?
I have absolutely no idea. I've been in the Zone for two weeks, I don't know every lunatic that's around here.
I see... Well, get lost while I'm still feeling generous.
No, please! Wait! Listen to what I have to tell you, please.
Alright, talk.

I can't just walk away. The guys who shot us didn't leave a single fucking trace whatsoever. Sultan's going to think I betrayed the crew or sold them out, and he'll bury me alive just like they did to Bill. I don't want that! Please, let me stay with you. I don't eat much and I can cook. Please!
Why should we let you stay? Wouldn't that bring us trouble with this Sultan?

Yeah... Fair point, it would cause trouble. But you could go over there and tell him we all died, then they wouldn't be looking for me. That'd be a relief. And I don't eat much, and if you bring me some tools I can repair your gear!
Fine, you can stay. But keep a low profile.
No. You'll only bring us trouble.
Thank you! You won't regret it. I promise I'll keep quiet and stay out of the way. And please, make sure you tell Sultan about our death. Nobody made it out of here alive. Remember that.
Alright. Take care of yourself.
Ah, damn. I'm a dead man. I'll get going then.
And don't come back.
...So you came to the Zone to be a bandit?
Nah, not at all. Let's just say I fell into the wrong crowd. They saw potential in me and steered me in that direction.
What potential did they see?

Well. I'm a good cook. I've got Italian roots, so I can make something delicious out of almost nothing. Although lately I was starting to doubt if the bandits didn't like me because of my abilities with the equipment. I'm good at stripping down weapons, polishing them, getting them clean and running like a charm. It's a nice hobby, you know?
I guess I'll put that to the test at some point.
So you're back. I hope you're bringing me something good.
Who are you? I don't recognize you, and unfortunately I know every loser in this base.
(Tell the truth) I'm Viktor. I'm looking for someone.
(Lie) Name's Tony, I'm a new recruit who's looking for someone.
(Lie) They call me Javier. I'm here on Barkeep's behalf.
(Lie) I'm Hernán. I know things that might interest you, we could trade valuable information.
(Tell the truth) I'm Viktor. Sidorovich sent me.
Viktor, huh. I've been hearing a lot about some newbie who's been causing problems all over Cordon. What a coincidence.
(Lie) Must be a different guy. I haven't been causing any problems.
(Tell the truth) That was probably me. I hope I haven't caused you too much trouble.
Interesting. They said it was a young, soft-spoken, still pretty green guy. Sounds like you...
No, no. I assure you it wasn't. Anyway, I need your help.
Yeah, yeah. Give me a moment. (Sultan throws a quick glance at the guards behind him)
I swear I'm not lying to you.
I appreciate someone who comes straight with me. It's a shame you really have caused me trouble, more than I can let slide. (Sultan throws a quick glance at the guards behind him)
Wait — I think we can work something out.
It's Tony, huh? I didn't see you in the last batch that came in. Which generation are you from?
(Dodge the question) Yeah, Tony. Italian roots. Where are you from, Sultan?
I asked you a question and you didn't answer. You think I'm stupid? (Sultan throws a quick glance at the guards behind him)
No, sorry. Could you remind me what you asked?
(Make something up) I'm from the latest batch, the best one yet.
So you're one of the seven from the last batch? Axe, Sparrow, Sly, Pirate, Short Fuse, Frank, and Purple. I don't remember any Tony in there.
Right... I made a mistake. I'm from the batch before that.
Javier? I wasn't expecting anyone, and the Barkeep usually pays upfront before sending someone. Why don't I know anything about this?
(Lie) He must have forgotten to tell you.
(Lie) Probably one of your guys didn't pass the message along.
So that's what it is. Never had this kind of problem before. Have a seat, make yourself comfortable. Let's talk. (Sultan throws a quick glance at the guards behind him)
(Turn to look at the guards)

You think so? They may be drunks and junkies, but they know who's got the biggest balls around here. And that's me. Sounds like you've got some pretty low expectations of my men... (Sultan throws a quick glance at the guards behind him) Boys, show him who runs things here.
(Turn to look at the guards)

%c[200,200,15,0] (Information minigame. Earn 5 points to win Sultan's favor) \n %c[default] I don't like information dealers, they think too highly of themselves. You sure Owl didn't send you? We haven't been on good terms since what happened in Zaton.
Of course not. I work alone. Information's too valuable to be gifting it to some associate.
Alright, give me something interesting first, and we'll see if I can help you after. What can you tell me?
I know a few more things...
Then tell me.
(Atreo) I have information about a stalker called Atreo.
I know him. Been trying to track him down for a while cause we don't want him near the base. What do you know?

He was hiding in Cordon. The stalkers ran him out of camp and he kept changing his name so nobody would shoot him on sight. They've been chasing him as far as the Dark Valley because his cover got blown out and he ran away. He's gotta be around here somewhere...

That son of a bitch... He owes me a lot of money. I doubt he'd dare show his face at the base, I know he screwed over some of my guys too. The man's got more than a few bounties on his head. What else do you know? Or was that it? %c[200,200,15,0] (+1 point)
(Mage) I know what happened to Andrés Mage.
Andrés Mage. I had respect for that man. A real shame he disappeared like that. What do you know about him?

He was killed in Cordon. A stalker named Wolf led a crew and hunted him down. After that, they stripped everything off him and took his PDA. Turns out the goods Mage used to trade were stolen from stalkers.

I already knew he was stealing — that's the beauty of buying cheap. But I didn't know about that idiot Wolf. About time someone gave him a forced retirement and got him out of the Zone for good. He's messed with my guys one too many times... I'll deal with that later. What else do you know? That last bit was interesting. %c[200,200,15,0] (+1 point)
(Screw) I heard about an artifact hunter who died recently.
Who? One of those under our protection?
He went by Screw. Died from radiation poisoning; or that's the suspicion, given how they found the body. His PDA mentioned that someone was tailing him, so I think he was killed.
Screw, huh? A great supplier and a solid example for stalkers. He paid us in artifacts and we kept him safe. A shame about Kolyan. What else do you know? That was useful. %c[200,200,15,0] (+1 point)
(Snob) I have information about the massacre at the southern farm.
Spit it out. I want to hear this.

I passed through there recently. Every bandit is dead, riddled with bullets by an unknown attacker. My guess is Monolith soldiers. I found a PDA with audio of Monolith soldiers shouting during the attack.

That's bad news. Those fanatics have been giving us a lot of trouble lately. You just reminded me that I need to double the guards on the West side. Do you know anything else about the Monolith? That was very useful. %c[200,200,15,0] (+1 point)
(Southern Monolith) I know things about the Monolith pushing into the Dark Valley.
Someone's been giving us trouble for a while now, and we don't know exactly who it is. You think it's those Monolith bastards?

There was a squad of them at the south of the Valley. Looks like they'd just came through Darkscape and were planning to take strategic positions. I ran into them with my crew and it seems like they're hunting someone. So they're here to stay.

Damn... (Sultan signals his men over your shoulder; a chill runs down your spine) Pass the word about those new defenses we were planning. Looks like things are about to get ugly. Anything else, Hernán? That information was very useful. %c[200,200,15,0] (+1 point)
(Kolyan) One of your bandits is shooting his own people at the base.
WHAT!? WHO THE HELL HAD THE NERVE TO OPEN FIRE UNDER MY NOSE!?
I saw a guy in the offices located on the south face of the building. I think his name's Kolyan. He cold bloodily executed a bandit who was running from him.

That Kolyan. This kind of thing can't happen under my protection. I'm afraid you know too much. (Sultan throws a quick glance at the guards behind him) First my subordinates do whatever they want, then I lose all authority, and next thing you know is some idiot tries to take power by putting a bullet in me while I sleep... %c[200,200,15,0] (-5 points)
Wait, I won't say a word.
I don't know anything else.
Somebody doesn't want to open their damn mouth. And I don't like that, cause you were doing so well. Shame. (Sultan throws a quick glance at the guards behind him)
Wait, I can tell you something else.
I don't know anything else. That's everything.

Good. I think you've earned my interest, Hernán. But before you ask me for anything, you'll need to do a favor for my organization. I need you to go talk to Kolyan, he's my right hand around here. He keeps the restless ones in line and takes some weight off my shoulders. \n Speak to him with respect, because he doesn't tolerate any kind of discourtesy... Well, you'll find that out yourself. We've run into some problems and I need someone capable to sort them out.
I can handle that. But then you'll help me with what I need.
Of course. But don't come back empty-handed. Do what I asked. If you don't, don't even think about showing your face around here again. Understood?
Understood. I'll be back when I'm done with Kolyan. Later.
Yeah, Viktor. The trader spoke to me about you and I unfortunately owe him a favor. But I've got some problems right now, so I can't help you at the moment. You'll have to wait a few weeks.
I don't have that much time. What's the problem? I'll help you fix it right now.

(Sultan smiles, satisfied) Now I understand why Sidorovich likes you... Listen, Viktor. My organization runs on four pillars. Kolyan is one; he helps me when making important calls and keeps the guys in line. Mage and Pirate were another pillar; they made sure we never ran short on resources. But there were problems recently and we're running low on firepower. Then there's me; I'm the one pulling all the strings...
And the fourth pillar?

The biggest coward you'll ever meet: the "Butcher", our doctor. He keeps people together, literally and figuratively... \n Not long ago, there was an expedition up North, near the Truck Cemetery. Kolyan was convinced we needed to take some points of interest up there, but the guys are scared of that place because of the mutants. So, they sent Butcher along to boost morale, but we lost contact with the group. I need to get that idiot back so things can run normally around the base. Go talk to Kolyan about this, he'll give you the details. I'm busy with something else right now.
Understood. As soon as this is sorted, we'll talk about how you can help me.
Good, we have a deal then. I hope you can sort it out fast. Watch yourself and don't get killed.
Yeah. See you.
I took care of what Kolyan asked.

Good. One or two problems down... Still about two hundred to go. (Sultan raises an eyebrow and frowns at you) What? Did you think leading a crew was easy? I've got a thousand things I need to handle just to keep it all from falling apart.
I didn't think anything out of line. I just did what you asked, and now it's your turn to do your part.

I like this kid. (Sultan speaks to the guards behind him and they laugh) He's got his balls in the right place. Now tell me what you need so we can sort it out right now. I don't like being in debt to anyone.
I'm looking for a stalker. Goes by Atreo. He's wearing a yellow jacket, stained with blood.
Atreo!? Why would you be looking for that son of a bitch on my turf? Don't tell me he had the nerve to come hide in the Dark Valley knowing I'm after him...
What do you know about him?

He's a compulsive liar. Years ago, he was a man you could rely on. He did his jobs on time and dealt with anyone who disrespected him right away. But one day he started hanging out with a group of mysterious stalkers and he went off the rails. He started making runs up North, going further and further each time, staying longer and longer... And every time he came back, he was thinner, more scarred, and less sane. Seems the more he learned about the Zone, the more unhinged he became.
Who was he traveling with?
Where exactly was he going?
Was he ever a bandit?
What did he learn about?

The guy was charismatic and could talk you into anything. They recruited him because they saw the talent in him. A group of three veteran stalker which I don't know their names very well, but I once saw them waiting for Atreo outside the bar... A very tall man with a gas mask; a beautiful woman in a white leather jacket; and a stalker with glasses, a bit hunched. Atreo left with them, and when he came back he wasn't the same. But he kept saying he had to go back North...
So he was traveling with three stalkers... I need to know more.

I know little about that. Here's how it went: he went away for two weeks and came back changed, but you could still hold a conversation with him. He told me about some lost mines up in the northern Zone, surrounded by reddish trees and a mysterious mutant watching him from a distance, whispering things to him. He looked disturbed. Then he was gone for a month, and when he came back, the poor bastard was so much thinner... I tried to talk to him, but he didn't listen; he was scattered and paranoid. He didn't want anyone to know what they were looking for...
Reddish trees and a mine... Could that be the Red Forest? I need to find out more.

Yeah. And a damn good one. The time we worked together we filled our pockets pretty well. He was the push I needed to start building a name for myself. We could've gone far together, but he had to go and lose his mind, the son of a bitch. His obsession with the North turned him into a lying piece of garbage; like a junkie, you know? You know any junkies? They blow all their money, and once it's gone, they start thinking they're smarter than everyone else and come up with more and more ridiculous lies. "I need to change my weapon," "I need an operation," "I need to get an artifact or I'm going to die," "There's a huge bounty on my head". Just wilder and wilder excuses to borrow money they'll never pay back. That's how it is, and I was an idiot for trusting him. I lent him a lot of money and he used it for another one of his ventures. Never saw him again, but he still owes me that money.
I suppose traveling for that many days gets expensive... I need to know more.

(Sultan taps his fingers under his chin as he tries to recall details) I know the people who recruited him were very knowledgeable, and once he was brought in, he became obsessed with places stalkers couldn't reach, strange artifacts, and the Monolith idiots. The last time we talked, he wouldn't stop going on about those damn Monolith. Later, I found out that one of them was looking for him, so he must have split from that group too and started going solo. Why? Did he find what he was looking for? Was it because of greed? Because of differences he had with them? I'd like to know that myself. \n A while back, when I was still trying to track him, I started paying for information. The bar's informant told me about a paranoid stalker, someone who didn't want to be followed and was rude to everyone. One day he got into a fight at the bar, got beaten up, and walked off, limping, through an anomaly field. No problem at all, like he was strolling through a forest. He didn't trigger a single anomaly. Some Duty guards saw it and they were speechless.
Pfft — someone immune to anomalies? That sounds like a campfire story. I'd like to ask them myself.
What else do you want to know?
I need help locating him. I know he's in the Dark Valley, running from me.

I've got three sentinels who gather information for me around the area, covering strategic spots. Go talk to them and see if they can help you with that. In the meantime I'll try to pull some strings and see if I can help you a little more with that matter of yours... One of them is in the tower near the south entrance of the base, the second is up on the structures at the west entrance, and the third you'll find on top of the gas station's storage tanks doing enemy reconnaissance. They must know something.
Good, I'll go talk to them then.

I almost forgot. I look after my own, don't think I don't value what you did for Butcher and Kolyan. You deserve this. \n Give Atreo my regards when you find him. If he's got any useful information, I'm willing to pay for it.
Well... Thank you. All of this is going to come in handy. I'll go talk to your sentinels.
(Kolyan hums an old song while looking at the map)
Hey. Sultan sent me to talk to you.
Hello Viktor. So you're going to go find our doctor? Good. You'll need a solid shotgun. If you don't have one, you should go see Pirate to gear up.
...How do you know my name?
I know a lot about you... But you're not ready for the answer to that question yet. We'll be able to talk about it properly when you find what you're looking for...
...Why a shotgun?

Our colleague got lost north of the Vehicle Cemetery, I'll mark the exact location on your PDA. The area is swarming with mutants that crawl and lurk behind the vehicles. The guys at the base call it the "Snork Yard" or the "Bandit Graveyard" as a joke, but it's more serious than a joke. Some of those bastards can take several shots from a good shotgun, so better go armed and with company.
Understood. I'll get myself a good barrel. Thanks for the heads-up.
So... why the mask?
Mine? Or yours?
I'll be the one with my face covered, but because that's me who we are talking about. While you sit in front of a screen... pretending to be something more.
...? Forget I asked.
(Kolyan starts laughing quietly)
I'm back. I brought Butcher, though it wasn't easy.
That's perfect. Here, I hope you can take this as both a payment and a token of friendship. I have a feeling you'll be coming to me again soon, with a lot of questions too.
Thank you for the artifact. What's next?

Don't mention it. Now, I have another task for you. It seems like there are anomalies behaving strangely in the Truck Cemetery. That's what Butcher's group originally went to investigate. But as you know, things didn't go well for them... I need a bit more control over that area, and you're going to give me a hand with that. The bandits are afraid to move around up there, but you went in and came back in one piece, so I think you can guide them. How do you feel about that?
Guide them? So you're putting me in charge of them?

That's a good question. Yes, you'd be in charge. Talk to Kashalot, the boys respect him. Ask him for some men to take along, the good ones, and move out. There are three locations I need you to sweep and clear of the mess the Monolith and the mutants have left behind. When you've done that, I'll tell Sultan you've done enough for us to owe you a huge favor.
Understood. I'll get men from Kashalot and go clear the graveyard.
In short, yes. I want the boys to see you doing it, they'll get to know someone important working alongside them. And they need to start getting familiar with your name.
Alright, I'll go see Kashalot. See you.
No stale bread here, beat it.
Kolyan sent me. I need some men for a raid.
But of course, your highness. Shall they come equipped with heavy artillery? Want them to be cracked snipers who could pick a hair off a frog? Whatever your lordship desires.

WHAT THE HELL DO I CARE IF KOLYAN SENT YOU!? WHO THE HELL DO YOU THINK YOU ARE, WALKING IN HERE AND ASKING FOR MEN LIKE IT AIN'T NOTHING!? I DON'T EVEN KNOW YOUR DAMN NAME, LOSER. YOU THINK THAT DOPEY FACE IS GONNA LEAD MY BOYS!? Tell me what the fuck you need people for. Where the fuck are you taking them?
We're going to the Truck Cemetery.

(Kashalot takes a breath to calm himself, then sighs) Interesting. They're sending people to die up North again? Already pulled that crap on me once, and now they're gonna do it again with some nobody as the leader... You know what? Fine. Let's go.
What do you mean, "let's go"?
Look at you all geared up, brother. Who'd you robbed?
Looks like the place is ours...
I think I owe you an apology. Here, my treat. Truth is, I was getting a little tired of Kolyan's insistence on send more guys to cover the bandit graveyard. Those guys were my brothers.
My condolences. Do you know why Kolyan's so interested in this dump?

He never gives details about nothing. A very cautious guy, and a crazy bastard. The guys who didn't wanna join the expeditions got shot by himself... I don't like that, but at least he commands respect. I've noticed he always tries to take places that are near anomalies. I think he's interested in artifacts, or in studying their appearance patterns, something like that. Why else would he be kidnapping scientists?
He kidnapped scientists!?

Hell yeah! The whole thing was a huge scandal. They even sent a military helicopter to kill us over it. I don't get why Sultan still holds him in such high regard, the man's a reckless, ruthless lunatic! But hey, that's his business. Honestly, I'd rather stay out here and get killed by cultists than be anywhere near him. And my advice to you is to stay as far away from his plans as you can. It's not gonna end well.

Hell yeah! The whole thing was a huge scandal. They even sent a military helicopter to kill us over it. I don't get why Sultan still holds him in such high regard, the man's a reckless, ruthless lunatic! But hey, that's his business. Honestly, I'd rather stay out here and get killed by cultists than be anywhere near him. And my advice to you is to stay as far away from his plans as you can. It's not gonna end well.
I understand. Thanks for the warning.

Thanks to you, brother. Turns out you're just like me, one of the 3G's: Good shooter, Good partner, and Good at looting bodies. HA! Take this, I'm getting a better weapon soon anyway. Hope you enjoy it. Get it tuned up with the mechanic and grab some good ammo, you'll feel the difference in caliber right away and you won't want to go back to 5.56. I guarantee that!
Damn... Thank you very much, Kashalot.
Don't mention it. Good luck with your stuff, and remember to stop by for a drink when you can. Things get boring around here, so count me in if you need someone to kick some ass.
See ya, Kashalot.
(Task) I'm looking for a stalker in a yellow jacket, stained with blood. Have you seen him around?
10.000 in cash and I'll tell you what I know.
Son of a... Sultan sent me, he said you'd talk. Check your messages.
(The bandit checks his PDA) Oh, shit. Well, I still didn't see anything. Sorry pal, you're gonna have to look on your own.
Thanks for nothing.
(Task) Sultan sent me. I'm looking for a stalker in a yellow jacket stained with blood. You seen him pass through?
No. Who'd be wearing a yellow jacket around here? You pullin' my leg or somethin'? Anyone who shows up looking like that is gettin' shot on sight. Ask someone else...
Understood. Thanks.
(Task) Sultan sent me. I'm looking for a stalker in a yellow jacket, stained with blood. Sounds weird I know, but I'm on his trail and I need to find him.
Sultan sent you? Wow, and nobody believed me last night. I saw the guy you're looking for. He was limping, frantic, and he was being chased by Monolith and some zombies.
Where did you last see him? What was he doing? I need to pick up his trail and fast.

He walked straight into the abandoned factory like it was nothing. There's an anomaly field in there that fries people's brains in seconds... Not even mutants go through there. Only the scientists Kolyan sends sometimes, they wander through in their protective suits.
Thanks! I have to go.

(Atreo mutters frantically) It rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me, it rejected me.
Who rejected you?
The artifact, it rejected me. We were getting along well, it was doing what I asked... I don't understand. After everything I had to go through, it rejected me.
I didn't know artifacts could reject their bearer.

(Atreo's eyes dart erratically in every direction instead of looking at you) This isn't an ordinary artifact. They have a will of their own, and you can only use their benefits if they allow it. I thought I was special, that I had been called and chosen to use them. All the visions, the noises, the screaming, the hunger, the information we found, the expeditions into God-forsaken places. All of it was a lie.
You had visions too?
What information did you find?
Who did you find that information with?
Where were these expeditions?

Yeah, many. I was tormented for months. Images came to me out of nowhere. I saw locations I'd never been to, as if I was supposed to do something there. Every time it happened, I'd taste old, intense blood in my mouth for hours. I'd hear people I'd never met all speaking at once, making it impossible to understand a fucking word; they even drowned out my own thoughts. But it all stopped when I got the artifact. I thought it was meant for me...

More information than any one person should know on their own. Have you looked what it's done to me? I can barely hold a conversation right now. I look like I've been mind-wiped by some fucking controller... \n I met with people who'd uncovered a great deal in the northern Zone. They'd found out there's a group capable of creating artifacts. They're not natural to the Zone, it's an unnatural intervention, and the result were these... things. (Atreo looks with contempt at the artifact in front of him) Those people knew a lot. I wanted to play their game and be part of it, but it backfired. I understand now that it's better not to get involved in certain things. I don't have much left...

The group called themselves "Pioneers"; they were three very strange stalkers. (Atreo coughs a little, looking affected) They were: Ozero, an engineer with exceptional skill with weapons and electronics, nearly two meters tall. He could take down a boar in a fistfight without breaking a sweat... Then there was Sova. She was the one with all the contacts. She got us access to resources, information, secrets. Everyone loved her, though I never quite understood why. She was always disconnected from reality, like if she was living in another world.
And the third stalker?

The worst one... Nox. There's very little reliable information about him and a lot of rumors, but I met him face to face and traveled with them. The man wore a Monolith suit and nobody EVER said a word about it, as if they couldn't see it or something. He was a genius with artifacts: he could walk through anomaly fields like they weren't there, he could do tricks with artifacts... yes, tricks! Once he took a fireball, pressed it in very precise spots, and launched a column of fire from his hands, like some kind of damn sorcerer! When he suspected we were being followed, he'd take some artifacts, activate them, and block the path with an anomaly field. Stalkers say anomalies shift position after every emission, but for me, it was always Nox.
"Was" a genius? What happened to him?

I don't know, and I doubt anyone does. But I have my suspicions... I think he flew too close to the sun. He played God with some artifacts and nobody ever saw him again. Though I doubt he's dead. His consciousness must be out there somewhere, haunting and tormenting people like us.

They already had several expeditions under their belt before I joined them. Together we visited three places: the Abandoned Hospital, the underground beneath Pripyat, and the "Southern" Village. The group seemed to have hints on some artifacts to be found in those locations, but we never found them in the end. The trips can be considered a failure.
